topic.name: The Internet & the World Wide Web

subtopics.name: The Internet & the World Wide Web

parts.problem_md:
**Explain **the differences between **HTTP **and **HTTPS**.

Include an **example **scenario where HTTPS would be preferred over HTTP
parts.solution_md:
The differences between HTTP and HTTPS include:

- HTTPS has an added layer of security **[1 mark]**
- All data sent and received using HTTPS is encrypted  **[1 mark]**
- HTTPS is used to protect sensitive information  **[1 mark]**
- **Any valid scenario** when HTTPS would be preferred over HTTP **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Examples may include:
> 
> - Accessing online banking websites
> - Entering login credentials
> - Any situation where sensitive information needs to be protected from unauthorised access

parts.problem_md:
A student visits a website that uses session cookies, instead of persistent cookies.

**Explain **the difference between session cookies and persistent cookies.
parts.solution_md:
The difference between a session and persistent cookie is:

Any **four **of the following:

- Session cookies are stored in memory/RAM **[1 mark]**
- … whereas persistent cookies are stored on the hard drive/secondary storage **[1 mark]**
- When the browser is closed a session cookie is lost **[1 mark]**
- … whereas a persistent cookie is not lost **[1 mark]**
- … until deleted by the user/they expire **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md: **Explain **why presentation is often separated from structure when creating a web page.
parts.solution_md:
Presentation is often separated from structure as:

Any **two **from the following:

- The formatting of the page can be changed/edited without needing to alter the structure **[1 mark]**
- … so, they can make regular updates without needing to check the structure **[1 mark]**
- The formatting document can be used again for a different website **[1 mark]**
- If further content and web pages are added to the website, the necessary formatting can be easily applied **[1 mark]**
- … so, this can save time when developing/updating a website **[1 mark]**
- Allows use of CSS to standardise formatting **[1 mark]**
- … so, CSS only needs to be created once (to be applied to each webpage) **[1 mark]**

A protocol is defined as:

Any **one **of the following:

- A set of rules **[1 mark]**
- … that governs communication between devices on a network **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
A student uses the internet for their schoolwork to research what is meant by pharming.

Storing **cookies **is one function of the web browser.

**Give three **other **functions **of the web browser.
parts.solution_md:
Example functions of a web browser include:

Any **three **of the following:

- Storing bookmarks/favourites **[1 mark]**
- Recording user history **[1 mark]**
- Allowing use of multiple tabs **[1 mark]**
- Providing navigation tools **OR** by example **[1 mark]**
- Providing an address bar **[1 mark]**
- Managing protocols **OR** by example **OR** checking digital certificate **[1 mark]**
- Send URL to DNS **[1 mark]**
- Sends a request to the IP address/web server (to obtain the contents of a webpage) **[1 mark]**
- Runs active script/JavaScript/client-side script **[1 mark]**
- Allows files to be downloaded from website/internet **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
Joelle is a student who uses the Internet

The table contains five terms or definitions that relate to the Internet

**Complete the table** by writing each missing term or definition.

| **Term** | **Definition** |
|---|---|
| browser |   |
|   | this is the company that provides a user with a connection to the Internet |
|   | this is a protocol that is used to send data for web pages across the Internet |
| Uniform Resource Locator (URL) |   |
| cookie |   |
parts.solution_md:
| **Term** | **Definition** |
|---|---|
| browser | **Software/application that allows users to view web pages / render HTML ****[1 mark]** |
| **Internet Service provider (ISP) ****[1 mark]** | this is the company that provides a user with a connection to the Internet |
| **HTTP OR HTTPS ****[1 mark]** | this is a protocol that is used to send data for web pages across the Internet |
| Uniform Resource Locator (URL) | **a text-based version of a web address ****[1 mark]** |
| cookie | **a text file (stored by web browser) that contains data about a user’s browsing habits/details/preferences ****[1 mark]** |

parts.problem_md:
Hexadecimal is used for Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) colour codes.

An HTML colour code is:

**#2F15D6**

Each pair of digits is stored as binary in an 8‑bit register

Websites can be created using HTML structure and presentation.

**State **what is meant by HTML **structure **and **presentation**.

**Give **an example of each in your answer
parts.solution_md:
HTML structure and presentation is:

**Structure **

- Layout of the web page **[1 mark]**
- Any valid example, e.g. Where text is placed **[1 mark]**

**Presentation **

- Formatting of the web page (accept: formatting/format of the elements) **[1 mark]**
- Any valid example, e.g. the colour of the font (accept: colour fonts) **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Don't confuse the two — structure is the layout/organisation of the page, presentation is its formatting; never define structure as 'the code'
> 
> Give a specific, clearly labelled example for each, and keep presentation examples about formatting features rather than content like images or links

parts.problem_md:
A web server has an internet protocol (IP) address.

The website has a uniform resource locator (URL)

An example of a URL is given.

[https://www.cambridgeassessment.org.uk/index.html](https://www.cambridgeassessment.org.uk/index.html)

**Complete the table** to identify the name of each section of the URL.

| **URL section** | **Name** |
|---|---|
| https |   |
| [cambridgeassessment.org.uk](http://cambridgeassessment.org.uk) |   |
| /index.html |   |
parts.solution_md:
| **URL section** | **Name** |
|---|---|
| https | protocol **[1 mark]** |
| [cambridgeassessment.org.uk](http://cambridgeassessment.org.uk) | domain name **[1 mark]** |
| /index.html | web page/file name **[1 mark]** |

parts.problem_md:
A student uses the internet for their schoolwork to research what is meant by pharming.

The student uses a **web browser** to access data on the internet.

**State **the purpose of the web browser.
parts.solution_md:
The purpose of a web browser is to:

- Display web pages **[1 mark]**
- … by rendering HTML **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Don't confuse the browser's purpose with networking tasks like DNS lookups or requesting data from servers
> 
> With two marks on offer, make sure you give two distinct points rather than one idea reworded
